question: Tell me about a time you worked significant overtime. How did you ensure you had recovery time afterward?

raiseTranscript.text: Tell me about a time you worked significant overtime. How did you ensure you had recovery time afterward?

Last sprint I stayed until 9pm three nights fixing a production incident on my own feature. I told my manager the next morning I needed the afternoon off to rest and she approved it. I also blocked my calendar the following week for shorter days.
What prompted you to ask for that time?
I had learned from a previous crunch that skipping recovery made me slower the next week, so I wanted to avoid repeating it.

raiseNotes: Q: Tell me about a time you worked significant overtime. How did you ensure you had recovery time afterward?
Junior IC on prod fix, 3 late nights
Asked manager next day for afternoon off + blocked lighter days
Follow-up: What prompted you to ask? Learned from prior crunch that skipping recovery hurt output
junior.raiseFeedback: Raises the bar on Respect time for a junior. The candidate described staying late on their feature incident and then proactively requesting afternoon off plus calendar blocks. Quote: 'I had learned from a previous crunch that skipping recovery made me slower the next week.' This shows ownership of personal sustainability at the expected individual scope. The example stays local but demonstrates coachability by applying past feedback. Biggest strength is the explicit link between overtime and planned recovery rather than hoping it would happen.

raiseTranscript.text: Tell me about a time you worked significant overtime. How did you ensure you had recovery time afterward?

Our cross-team migration slipped and I worked late for a week coordinating fixes. I told the other leads I would take two days of focused work time the following week and asked them to shield me from new asks. I also redistributed some of my on-call shifts.
They were fine once I explained the recovery was to keep me effective for the handoff.

senior.raiseFeedback: Raises the bar on Respect time for a senior. The candidate worked late on a cross-team migration and then secured focused recovery days plus on-call relief by influencing peers. Quote: 'I told the other leads I would take two days of focused work time the following week.' This shows influence without authority and metrics (protecting handoff quality) expected at senior level. The story extends beyond individual scope. Biggest strength is treating recovery as a team coordination item rather than a personal request.

raiseTranscript.text: Tell me about a time you worked significant overtime. How did you ensure you had recovery time afterward?

During a major reorg I worked late for two weeks finalizing org design and risk mitigation. I then blocked the following week for no meetings and delegated all but two decisions to my directs, telling them this was to model sustainable leadership at scale.
Two quarters later my directs started doing the same after their own crunch periods, which reduced escalations to me.
